newsitem.title: USA: N.Dakota flooding blamed on wetlands destruction.
newsitem.headline: N.Dakota flooding blamed on wetlands destruction.

text.p: Wetlands destruction in the Red River valley of North Dakota and Minnesota worsened the damage from record floodwaters that inundated the region this spring, environmentalists said Tuesday.

If the river's watershed had not lost 75 percent of its original wetlands, which act as nature's sponges, the Red River might not have topped levees in Grand Forks and other towns in the region, the Sierra Club said.
The Sierra Club's Brett Hulsey presented a news conference with his report on wetlands destruction and the flooding that swamped the northern plains.
Hulsey recommended restoring wetlands, moving flood-prone homes, and ending policies that make it easy to get permits to drain wetlands for farming or development.

Restoring just six percent of the Red River basin's wetlands at an estimated cost of $250 million would have stored 20 days of Grand Forks' peak flood flow, the report said. The city sustained more than $1 billion in damage from last month's flooding.
